plainTranslation:
This connection can feel like a constant back-and-forth between the practical idea and the wild one.

One person may take the grounded position: what makes sense, what can be proven, what works in real life. The other may push toward the new angle, the strange possibility, the thing that has not been tried yet. The roles can switch, but the tension stays. Together, you keep each other from getting too rigid or too unmoored.

The attraction is mental. This person makes your mind work harder. They may challenge your opinions, sharpen your ideas, or make you defend what you think. That can be frustrating, but it can also be exciting. Easier people may be calmer to talk to, but they may not stretch you the same way.

The trouble is that the back-and-forth can go on forever without landing anywhere.

One of you asks for evidence. The other asks for imagination. One wants the idea to make sense now. The other wants room for what is not yet possible. Under stress, both of you may move to extremes. The practical one becomes more rigid. The radical one becomes more extreme. Then the middle disappears.

A disagreement about an idea can also turn into a fight about respect. It stops being about the topic and starts becoming about whose mind counts.

This aspect works best when you respect how the other person thinks, not only what they think. Disruption can be intelligence. Practical thinking can be wisdom. Without that respect, the connection becomes a contest.

Let some differences stay unresolved. Not every conversation needs a winner. Take turns leading. One day, stay practical. Another day, follow the wild idea. Keep a few agreements of care that do not change, even when every idea is up for debate.

The person who challenges your mind the most may also be the person who helps it grow.
